 Thales has a vacancy for a Senior Project Buyer to support the AJISS Engineering Changes Team across the Arctic and Offshore Patrol Ship In-Service Support (AJISS) program. As a Senior Project Buyer, you will translate engineering change requirements into purchasable, executable work packages—ensuring Purchase Orders (POs) are issued on time, supplier commitments are aligned to delivery and milestone expectations, and risks/issues are identified early and resolved decisively. You will also increase organizational knowledge by mentoring, improving practices, and strengthening end-to-end purchasing/supply execution. You will act as an experienced and independent owner for purchasing execution and supply readiness that enables engineering change delivery and act as the interface between the AJISS engineering team, procurement, and suppliers, ensuring projects meet their targets, risks are managed, and communication remains transparent.
 Regulatory Compliance Requirement 
 This position requires direct or indirect access to hardware, software or technical information controlled under the Canadian Export Control List and /or the US the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). All applicants must be eligible or able to obtain authorization for such access.
 Key Areas of Responsibility 
 Own end-to-end AJISS engineering-change procurement/supply execution: manage sourcing, PO creation/issuance, supplier documentation, and ensure technical/contractual alignment (scope, quantities, specs, terms, lead times, quality/compliance, delivery). 
 Drive schedule and milestone performance: track work package progress, proactively identify risks (lead time slippage, capacity, technical clarifications, documentation readiness), and lead recovery actions/escalations to protect AJISS deliverables. 
 Manage defense-approved/program-relevant suppliers: build and maintain relationships, support readiness and delivery planning, and ensure suppliers meet commitments for delivery dates, quality, and required documentation. 
 Serve as cross-functional purchasing interface: partner with engineering, program/project management, category management, quality, operations, finance, legal, and bid/capture; provide transparent status, forecasts, and risk reporting with timely escalation. 
 Run post-award supplier execution & performance management (where applicable): monitor delivery performance, execute supplier recovery/containment support, conduct performance reviews, and ensure corrective actions are initiated, tracked, and verified. 
 Support change governance and continuous improvement: represent procurement interests in change review boards and cross-functional meetings; continuously improve purchasing/supply execution workflows to reduce cycle time, rework, and schedule variance (including lessons learned and templates). 
 Ensure compliance and audit-ready evidence: maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready records of orders, compliance artifacts, correspondence, and acceptance evidence; ensure all interactions meet contractual, ethical, and regulatory requirements. 
 Escalate and lead resolution of systemic issues: identify root causes of purchasing/supply bottlenecks and propose practical mitigations (alternative suppliers, revised delivery sequencing, PO scope/terms updates, revised recovery plans). 
 Be a go-to resource and (where needed) mentor others: support the team proactively, reduce friction between functions, and share process knowledge/best practices. 
 Engagement Points:
 Internal: 
 Work Package Manager (WPM) / Project Manager (PM): alignment on scope, schedule, risks, issues, and supplier performance; ensure purchasing actions support recovery and commitment management. 
 Engineering Design Manager (EDM) / Engineering: Collaborate to clarify technical requirements, manage Statement of Work (SoW) deliverables, and ensure seamless management of technical interfaces. 
 Procurement / Category Management: Ensure sourcing strategies are aligned, coordinate handover from pre-award activities, and provide feedback on supplier performance for future sourcing decisions. 
 Project Manager: Track and forecast costs, support and manage budgets/EAC, and control milestones and payments related to supplier contracts. 
 Quality / Safety / RAM / Industrial / Operations: Monitor and manage supplier performance in quality, safety, industrialization, compliance and timely delivery. 
 Legal / Commercial: Support contract variations, claims, disputes, and escalations, ensuring adherence to contractual and legal requirements. 
 Bid / Capture Teams: Provide insights on supplier performance, risks, and costs to inform bids and proposals for future projects. 
 External: 
 Key suppliers / subcontractors: Manage day-to-day commercial, and performance relationships to ensure project success. 
 Customer representatives (where appropriate): Coordinate supplier-related matters impacting project delivery and customer commitments. 
 Auditors or regulatory bodies (as required): Provide evidence of supplier compliance with contractual, ethical, and regulatory requirements. 
 Minimum Qualifications 
 8+ years’ relevant experience in procurement, supply chain, commercial or contract management, with clear exposure to post award supplier management.
 Experience in procurement or supply chain within the defense or high-compliance industry, ideally supporting in-service support or engineering change programs.
 Strong project management and milestone tracking skills using relevant tools (e.g., SAP, MS Project).
 Excellent supplier engagement and relationship management abilities.
 Proactive risk identification and mitigation skills; able to challenge delays constructively.
 Effective communicator in cross-functional, high-stakes environments.
 Working knowledge of defense industry regulations, government contracting, and AJISS program requirements is highly desirable.
 The candidate must meet all the following criteria:
 a) possess a university degree in any field and possess a minimum of 2 years of demonstrated experience in a procurement and finance related activity within the last 5 years or possess a diploma from a recognized college program in procurement, finance, economics, commerce, accounting or materiel management and possess a minimum of 3 years of demonstrated experience in a procurement and finance related activity within the last 6 years; and 
 All applicants must be able to obtain a Canadian NATO Secret clearance and meet the eligibility requirements outlined in the Canadian Controlled Goods Registration Program and ITAR. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Professional qualifications or training in one or more of the following: Procurement / supply chain (e.g. CIPS or equivalent)
 Project management (e.g. PRINCE2, APM or equivalent)
 Commercial / contract management
 Degree (or equivalent experience) in business, commercial, engineering or related discipline.

 Customer focused, delivering on commitments to internal and external stakeholders.
 Collaborative, building strong relationships across functions and with suppliers.
 Accountable, taking ownership for outcomes and driving issues to resolution.
 Agile, adapting quickly to changing priorities, scope and constraints.
 Innovative, seeking continuous improvement in supplier performance and ways of working.
 Ethical and transparent, acting with integrity in all supplier interactions.

 Role will require working from both office (3) and home (2) (hybrid).
 Schedule: 40 working hours per week Monday- Friday. Flexible time, however, accommodating core hours of 9 am-3 pm, project needs and global/international time zones.

 Job Description: 
 Are you passionate about computing and AI accelerators?
 Do you thrive on innovation and want to disrupt the industry? Are you eager to work with leading AI hardware engineers on Intel's latest architecture? If you love collaborating with diverse teams to create best-in-class AI compute platforms, Intel's GPE department has exciting opportunities for you.
 As a member of the GPE team, you will develop hardware and platform solutions for Intel products, including the newest IPs targeted at next-generation GPUs and AI accelerators. 
 You will have the opportunity to engage in enabling technologies in PCB design, manufacturing, testing, and debugging. We are a winning team with a clear vision of delivering competitive and cutting-edge products, and we are committed to building the best products and developing the best skills for our team.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Work on end-to-end power delivery design and development, from initial concept to implementation of power delivery requirements and ecosystem enabling power integrated circuits.
 Own power integrity simulation for the platform power delivery network: build and correlate VRM-to-die PDN models, run DC IR-drop and AC target-impedance analysis, and perform transient droop and Ldi/dt studies across die, package, and PCB to set the decoupling and stack up strategy before layout is committed.
 Apply knowledge of power conversion topologies, including components, compensation circuits/stability analysis, drop/droop analysis, simulation tools , and techniques, as well as PCB layout and design tools, to characterize performance and validate correlation of simulation modeling and results.
 Design and validate platform power conversion and management solutions, including energy management, and perform simulation and optimization for package and PCB, including stack up, power/ground noise plane assignment, decoupling solutions, and/or power sequencing requirements.
 Design for debug: architect observability into the board from the start, including per-rail voltage and current sense points, Kelvin-sense and probe landing points, telemetry and current-monitor access (SVID/PMBus/IMON), rail-level isolation and enable control, and voltage-margining , so power-on and post-silicon issues can be isolated on the first board instead of a respin.
 Design for flexibility: build configurability into the power delivery solution so a single board can support multiple SKUs and derivatives, using stuffing options for phase count and decoupling, pin-compatible dual-source regulator footprints, rail split/merge and current headroom for higher-power SKUs, and programmable load line, compensation, and VID range.
 Create and execute test plans to validate and characterize power delivery solutions.
 Correlate bench and VR test tool measurements with simulation results to improve simulation model accuracy and close the loop on power integrity assumptions.
 Conduct failure analysis and root cause investigations for power delivery issues, implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
 Collaborate with silicon and platform architects to generate solutions and analyses, delivering content into platform design guides as solution collaterals for end customers.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including board design, SW/FW, and systems validation, to ensure seamless integration of power delivery solutions.
 Qualifications: 
 Minimum Qualifications , you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
 5+ years of experience in:
 Designing low voltage, high current, multi-phase DC-DC switching regulators (buck, boost, etc.) to meet stringent targets, optimizing the design for transient response and conversion efficiency. 
 Working with signal/power integrity and power delivery network simulation tools such as Cadence Sigrity PowerDC/PowerSI, Ansys SIwave etc. to develop accurate models of circuit design  
 Design and optimize accurate power delivery simulation models using SPICE and time-based simulation tools (LTSpice, SIMPLIS etc.) based on SOC design power requirements. 
 Power delivery network modeling across die, package, and PCB, including stackup, plane assignment, decoupling network design, and S-parameter extraction and correlation.
 Experience using oscilloscopes and DAQ for hardware troubleshooting and debugging.
 Interacting with Signal Integrity, Layout, and Mechanical engineers, with working knowledge of SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical aspects of board designs.
 Preferred Qualifications, are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.
 Experience designing for debug and testability on power delivery hardware, including sense and telemetry instrumentation, voltage margining, and rail isolation for post-silicon bring-up.
 Experience designing configurable power delivery solutions that support multiple SKUs and derivative products from a single board design.
 Identify new technologies/interfaces and develop board power delivery architecture.
 Experience in project management, including leading projects and manage timelines and resources effectively.
 Familiarity with emerging technologies such as GaN power devices, switched capacitor topology, etc.
 Experience delivering products for high-volume production and cost optimization.
 Knowledge of board and power management (HW/SW/FW) debugging.
 Willing to provide hardware technical support to ODM/OEM board vendors.
 Willingness to travel globally to meet internal teams and external customers.

 An overview of this role 
 As a Staff Regional Marketing Manager, you will own regional marketing for the sales team in your territory and set the standard for how the regional team plans and runs its work. You will choose, plan, and run the events and campaigns that create, expand, and accelerate pipeline in your region, and you will move easily between high-level strategy and creative, detailed execution. Staff is a leadership-level individual contributor role: you lead through the work you build and ship, not through direct reports. In a modern marketing organization, that means building and running your own plans, programs, measurement, and AI-assisted automation instead of handing them off, and it suits builders who are comfortable being a leader without a team to manage. Your audience is CIOs, CTOs, VPs of engineering and platform, and the security leaders who govern how their teams ship software. You will judge audience quality by seniority and buying role, not headcount, so you will need to understand how they work and what they want from a vendor.

As a senior individual contributor, you will mentor other regional marketers, help build and improve team process, and share best practices with regional peers by planning and operating transparently. Your impact is measured in pipeline: the target is 10X spend contribution to sales pipeline for your region, with your regional budget spent within 5% variance.  Drive results for your region as its marketing leader: own the pipeline and growth outcomes, and go beyond events and experiences to bring partners in to drive marketing across channels, in support of growth through our revenue team.

 Set regional event and campaign strategy, with discretion over which events and campaigns best support regional sales goals, and manage events onsite, including logistics, booth staffing, and swag.

 Support Channel and Alliance Marketing activities with GitLab partners, from campaign approval through execution.
 Work with external agencies and third parties to prepare, manage, and execute campaigns.
 Mentor and guide regional marketing specialists and managers, and lead in building and driving process within the team.

 Proven ability to build and execute a regional strategy, with a record of delivering, accelerating, and expanding sales pipeline through regional marketing.
 Experience supporting both direct sales and channel sales teams, and in enterprise solution demand creation and regional marketing.
 Exemplary analytical skills and a proven aptitude for using data to optimize program performance and inform future strategies.

WANTED: One Hungry Closer Who's Sick Of Selling Other People's Dreams. 
 (Read this whole thing. If you quit halfway, we already have your answer.) 
 Most job ads read like they were written by HR. 
Bullet points. Buzzwords. 
A "competitive compensation package" that translates to "we'll pay you just enough to keep you from leaving, but never enough to actually win." 
 This isn't that.
 This is a letter. From us to you. About one of the most lopsided opportunities we've ever put in front of a salesperson and the rare, specific human being we're trying to find to fill it.
 If that human is you, you're going to feel it in your chest somewhere around paragraph nine.
 First — Who We Are. And Why It Matters. 
 We're Wealth Without Wall Street. 
 Russ Morgan and Joey Muré built this from scratch, not in a Manhattan glass tower, not with a hedge-fund pedigree, but by getting fed up watching hardworking business owners hand their financial futures to suit-wearing strangers who couldn't pick them out of a lineup.
 Together we've helped thousands of business owners, real estate investors, doctors, and high-earning professionals do what 99% of America has been brainwashed into believing is impossible:
 Generate passive income that exceeds their monthly expenses. 
 That's the whole game. That's what freedom actually looks like — not a 401(k) you can't touch until you're 65 and your knees are gone, but real cash flowing in every single month whether you work or not.
 We do it using the Infinite Banking Concept — the same wealth strategy quietly used by the richest families in America for over a century. We teach people to become their own bank. To recycle their capital. To stop renting money from institutions that profit off their ignorance.
 Russ and Joey have done it themselves. Over $50,000 per month in passive income. Co-authors of an Amazon bestseller. Hosts of one of the most respected podcasts in personal finance.
 This isn't theory. This is the real thing.
 Right now, we have more qualified people waving their hands than we can possibly talk to.
 That's where you come in.
 The Role: Business Developer. (Translation: The Person Who Decides Who Gets Free.) 
 Let us describe a typical day so you know exactly what you're signing up for.
 You wake up. You check your calendar. There are real, pre-qualified humans on it, people who registered for our workshops, devoured Russ and Joey's content, raised their hand, and said "I want a Passive Income Game Plan Session." 
 These aren't cold strangers. 
These aren't leads scraped off a list. 
These are people who already trust the brand, already believe the philosophy, and already know they're tired of the rat race.
 Your job is to pickup the phone, set appointments by making outbound calls and take inbound appointments.
Ask the kind of questions most salespeople are too soft to ask. 
Find out where they really are financially, emotionally, mentally. Diagnose whether IBC and our path is actually right for them.
 And if it is? You hand them the keys.
 You're not pitching. You're not pressuring. You're not chasing.
 You're the bridge between someone's current life — exhausted, overworked, financially fragile — and the version of their life where they sleep through the night because money is finally working for them instead of against them.
 That's the job.
 If that sounds like too much responsibility, the back button is right there.
 Who We Are NOT Looking For. 
 Let's save us both some time.
 We are not looking for the guy who calls himself a "closer" because he sold timeshares in Cabo for six months.
 We are not looking for the person who needs a six-week ramp, a personal coach, three resource Slack channels, and a "psychologically safe" environment to dial a phone.
 We are not looking for someone who's going to ghost on Friday afternoons because the surf is up.
 We are not looking for a salary chaser. If a guaranteed paycheck is what you're after, McDonald's is hiring. Go thrive.
 And we are definitely not looking for someone who can't speak from the heart about money, freedom, and the very real fear most Americans carry around about both. If you can't connect at the soul level, you can't sell this. Period.
 Who We ARE Looking For. 
 A killer. But a killer with a conscience.
 Someone who can sit across a Zoom screen from a stranger and — within ten minutes — have them admitting things they haven't told their spouse.
 Someone who's already a top performer somewhere else and is bored to tears selling SaaS, solar, or something else they couldn't care less about.
 Someone who reads Rich Dad Poor Dad , listens to BiggerPockets, follows Dave Ramsey just to argue with him, and already has an opinion about whole life insurance — even if that opinion needs updating.
 Someone with the spine to say "I don't think you're a fit. Here's why," and walk away from money on principle.
 Someone who treats every conversation like it's their last shot — because that's how the great ones do it.
 If you read those five paragraphs and felt seen, keep going.
 The Non-Negotiables.
 Proven sales background. Minimum 2+ years closing in a high-ticket, phone/Zoom-based environment. We don't care about your resume — we care about your numbers.
 25%+ close rate after probation. Below that, you're not the right fit and we'll part as friends.
 Full ownership of your pipeline. Nobody is going to chase you to follow up. The leads are there. The CRM is built. The systems work. You just have to work them. 
 Show up sharp every single day. This is a high-tempo environment. We move. We measure. We adjust.
 Live the message. If you don't believe building wealth outside the traditional system is possible, you cannot sell it. Period. Bonus points if you already own a whole life policy, have read Becoming Your Own Banker by Nelson Nash, or have personal experience with real estate investing or passive income.
 Stable, professional remote setup. High-speed internet, quiet environment, quality camera and mic. We're representing a premium brand on every single call.

MID-MARKET IMPLEMENTATION SPECIALIST

Hi! I'm Daryl, and I'm the Manager of High Touch (Mid-Market) Implementations at Ashby. One of my favorite things about this team is that we're the first real proof point for a new customer; from day 1, we get the hands-on opportunity to show them why they made the right call switching to Ashby.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we added more than 2,100 new customers in the last year alone and now support over 5,000 customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. We're expecting similarly fast growth this year, and every one of those new customers needs a thoughtful implementation to actually get value out of Ashby. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're expanding this team!




THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Mid-Market Implementation Specialist who excels at leading technically complex, hands on implementation projects for B2B SaaS customers. You'll own each implementation from the moment Sales hands it off through go-live; part project manager, part technical expert, and part trusted advisor to the customer!

Six months in, success looks like carrying a full book of 15-20 active implementations, running each customer relationship on your own (kickoff, timeline, follow-through), independently solving complex configuration and workflow challenges, and handling the normal bumps (a slow-to-respond customer, a technical snag, an escalation) without the rest of your book slipping. It also means you're starting to make things better beyond your own accounts: you've found at least one process or documentation gap and fixed it, and you're feeding real customer feedback back to our Product team.




YOU WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY:

 - Managing 15-20 active mid-market implementations at a time (8-10 weeks implementation timeline on average), building each customer's project plan from handoff through go-live, and staying on top of timelines, hurdles, and follow-up along the way

 - Getting genuinely comfortable with the in’s and out’s of how our products work, so you can troubleshoot and advise instead of just walking through a checklist

 - Advising on what’s worked well for similar customers in the past, challenging assumptions when appropriate, and recommending configurations and workflows that balance customer needs with implementation best practices

 - Partnering closely with cross-functional partners across the business, especially Sales and CS to ensure a seamless customer journey, and Product/Engineering to flag real issues and align on a path forward

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who gets energy from both sides of this: the structure of running a tight project plan, and the judgment to rethink that plan when a customer's business genuinely calls for it.



If you have the majority of the following, you could be a great fit for this role: 

 - 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing role, with the majority of your focus on leading full-cycle B2B SaaS implementations

 - Proven track record successfully managing concurrent mid-market implementation projects without compromising quality, customer experience, or timelines

 - Experience operating with real autonomy and to own the implementation project plans end-to-end

 - Comfortable getting into the weeds of complex, multi-module software, and building genuine fluency in how it all fits together

 - Resourceful when there's no documented answer; you do your own testing and discovery, then use what you learn to advise customers on best practices and recommendations

 - Data-driven and detail-oriented, with a genuine instinct for coaching customers through unfamiliar territory

If you need someone else to do any of the following, then this role is probably not for you:

 - Independently investigate complex customer questions and become the technical/product subject matter expert during implementations

 - Carry more than a handful of accounts at once (this is a high volume role on a team that moves with urgency)

 - Own the execution of a project plan, not just its design

 - Iterate and improve on existing processes




ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website:  https://www.ashbyhq.com/%EF%BF%BC%EF%BF%BCWehttps://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀




INSTRUCTIONS

Please take your time with your application and the application questions. Although we use AI to assist in our review, we never use AI to auto-qualify or disqualify candidates. We lay eyes on each and every application, and speak to a very select number of candidates based on the application as a whole. This is an evergreen opening, so there is no need to rush, and there are no prizes for being first!




OUR PHILOSOPHY

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

 - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

 - We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles to get a sense of what we are looking for in folks on the team.




THE INTERVIEW

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

 - 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

 - 45 min - Interview with Manager of High Touch Implementations

 - 60 min- Mock Call with an Implementation Specialist and Customer Success Manager

 - Final Round:
   
   - 30 min - Cross-Functional Interview with Head of Professional Services
   
   - 30 min - Product Complexity Interview with VP of Customer Success
   
   - 30 min - Customer Adoption & Enablement with Manager of High Touch Customer Success and a High Touch Customer Success Manager
   
   - 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager




BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - You get to sell a product that our prospects & customers are truly excited about.

 - Competitive compensation is offered.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 I. Scope and Summary of Primary Responsibilities 
 In covering a broad range of duties responsibilities include completing initialinterview, ongoing assessment and therapy of children birth to school age with vision loss to identify rehabilitation goals and develops service plan to address goals with families. This position also develops individual intervention and therapy programs in accordance with goals. It also assists the child’s family to access available resources to address their vision needs. This position also facilitates a child’s transition into community and school programs.
 This position provides functional expertise for the comprehensive multi-faceted service and operationsprogram within a matrix reporting structure.  
 II. Essential Functions 
 This position entails, but is not limited to the following:
 General Responsibilities: 
 ·       Conducts/or participates in an initial and ongoing assessments for children aged, birth to school entry, with vision loss.  Assists child, family and community team in developing rehabilitation goals.
 ·       Develops and/or contributes to Individual Family Service or Intervention Plan developed by the local community IE Team to assist children with vision loss in developing motor, visual, cognitive, self-care, social, literacy and sensory skills in accordance with vision rehabilitation goals.
 ·       Evaluates child’s progress to revise service plans and implement programs that address client and family needs.
 ·       Assesses environmental conditions, accessibility and safety in settings that the child encounters (home, preschool, playgrounds, etc.)
 ·       Provides support and information to parents and caregivers on methods and techniques for helping to overcome barriers to inclusion. Provides support and information to parents/caregiver to enhance advocacy skills.
 ·       Acts as a consultant/resource to the professional and service community regarding issues pertaining to children with vision loss including children with additional disabling conditions.
 ·       Provides interventions and supports to the child and family in the form of: direct intervention; resources and information; collaboration with other programs and service providers; presentations; and transition planning.
 ·       Completes required documentation including assessments, progress reports, statistics on service delivery, etc.
 ·       Keeps abreast of current materials, technology, standards of practice related to providing service to children with vision loss by review of professional literature, attending conferences/workshops and accessing other current sources of information
 Relationships 
 ·       Interacts with children, their family, caregivers, and community team to develop and identify vision related goals and develop early intervention and therapy programs, and support families to follow through on recommendations. 
 ·       Works closely and collaboratively with key partner organizations.
 ·       Builds and maintains good working relationships with professionals in other agencies and community groups, particularly others on the child’s therapy team.
 ·       Educates stakeholders about VLRC and its specialized programs offered to children and their families and the importance of early intervention. 
 ·       Works as a multi-disciplinary team and participates in team meetings.
 ·       Advocates on child’s behalf in medical clinics, schools, etc. when possible.
 ·       Instructs and supervises volunteers and students (and Occupational Therapy Assistants where applicable) to work with children.
 Problem Solving/Time Frame of Impact 
 ·       Position utilizes problem solving abilities related to implementing and developing intervention and therapy programs for children with vision loss.
 ·       Problem solving involved in adapting programs, materials and equipment to address the needs of children with complex health conditions.  
 ·       In case of critical incidents such as indications of child abuse or medical emergencies the Occupational Therapist must immediately report concerns and ensure children are receiving appropriate care.  Procedure varies by province. 
 ·       Must be able to work with a child’s family recognizing their complex needs including; cultural, religious, mental health needs and/or emotional support.
 Decision Autonomy 
 ·       Decision making based on training and experience working with children with visual impairments, and individual assessment and reassessment, to develop an appropriate service plan.
 ·       Judgment is utilized for making decisions about method, schedule, and type of assessment and treatment and the manner in which parents are taught to follow through on recommendations.
 ·       This position is itinerant, requiring frequent visits to family homes.
 Leadership 
 ·       Provides leadership and guidance when training and supervising volunteers, parents, students and community.
 ·       Takes initiative to develop/implement the most appropriate intervention for client and in maintaining current knowledge associated with children with vision loss.

 ·       Demonstrated understanding of vision loss in children is an asset

 ·       Excellent communications and interpersonal skills
 ·       Ability to build trusting relationships with children and families
 ·       Experience supervising volunteers and support personnel an asset
 ·       Ability to utilize computer and software programs.
 ·       Excellent facilitation skills both in groups and individual situations
 ·       Good organization and time management skills.
 Experience and Education:

 ·       Knowledge of normal and abnormal early childhood development.
 ·       3 or more years experience working with children with vision loss as well as children with additional disabling conditions is an asset.

The Automations Platform team builds the system that lets Jobber Teammate, our AI teammate for home service businesses, do a service provider's work for them. Every automation in Jobber runs on what this team builds.



The role:

You'll make it possible for Jobber Teammate to automate every task in Jobber.

Today a handful of automations exist and each one is expensive to build. The ambition is that every task a service provider repeats in their week has an automation that does it for them. Getting there takes two things at once, and this role does both.

You'll build the platform: the authoring, execution and evaluation models that let any product team at Jobber ship an automation without first becoming AI specialists. Skill files, tool calls, and evals that make an automation measurably better over time.

You'll also build on the platform: choosing the automations that matter most, shipping them yourself, and making them easy to find, enable and trust. Being the platform's hardest customer is what keeps it honest.

Over time you'll open it up, so service providers create their own and the best ones spread to businesses like theirs.

This suits someone equally at home in an architecture discussion and a customer interview.



As Senior Product Manager you will:

 - Build a deep understanding of home service businesses and the repeated work that consumes their week.

 - Own the automation platform: how automations are authored, how they execute, and how they're evaluated and improved.

 - Make it fast and cheap for any Jobber team to ship an automation, and measure yourself on their throughput rather than your own.

 - Build the highest-impact automations yourself, and make them easy for service providers to find, enable and trust.

 - Build an Evals platform, that makes it easy to iterate on and improve automations so the quality bar is constantly raising

 - Bring the product requirements to our AI Foundations engineering team, who build the underlying agent infrastructure.

 - Define the metrics that tell you the platform works: cost and speed of building an automation, engagement with the ones we ship, and growth of the library.

 - Experience building an AI platform was genuinely adopted - won through advocacy, tooling, and documentation.

 - Experience shipping LLM-backed or ML-backed products, with real respect for how they fail.

 - A track record of making a contested technical decision and making it stick.

 - Comfort thinking in unit economics, because the cost of building an automation decides whether this strategy is real.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development. Can You Spot An Influencer Who’ll Actually Sell? You know that good partnerships don’t just “create buzz.” They drive revenue, build authority, and make competitors wonder how the heck you’re everywhere at once. You know how to build a scalable affiliate program where the right partners drive sales, the right experts build trust, and every campaign has the tracking and reporting to prove it.
If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to be the Senior Influencer and Partnerships Specialist at AlgaeCal.
 Small Print ⇒ If you think influencer marketing is about collecting “likes” this role isn’t for you. We’re looking for someone who can build a performance-driven partnership ecosystem, manage creators and affiliates, negotiate smart deals, and sniff out wasted spend faster than a bloodhound chasing a runaway sausage cart.
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. The creators, affiliates, and experts you bring into our world will help women find information they can trust, feel more confident in their choices, and take action on their health.
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You know how to find the right partners. A creator with 500,000 followers doesn’t automatically make your pulse race. You look at audience fit, engagement, credibility, brand alignment, and whether there’s a realistic path to revenue. You’re not here to collect vanity metrics. You’re here to build a pipeline of influencers, creators, affiliates, and healthcare experts who can actually perform.
 You’re comfortable working with performance data. ROAS, CAC, conversion rate, attributed revenue, and performance by partner aren’t things you leave for someone else to figure out. You know how to read the data, spot what’s working, kill what isn’t, and put more money behind the partnerships that deserve it.
 You know how to build strong relationships. Great partnerships aren’t built by firing over a contract and resurfacing three months later asking for a report. You know how to build trust, communicate clearly, create offers people actually want to say yes to, and keep good partners wanting to work with us again. From first conversation to signed agreement to live campaign to reporting, you know how to keep the whole thing moving.
 You understand how affiliate programs work. You’re not the kind of person who opens Impact and stares hopefully at the dashboard. You understand recruitment, activation, commission structures, incentives, optimization, and what it takes to turn a handful of affiliates into a real growth channel. Experience with Impact, Klear, GRIN, Shopify Affiliates, or similar platforms will definitely come in handy.
 You know how valuable the right expert can be. Healthcare professionals and science experts aren’t there to make the About Us page look impressive. The right expert can build trust, strengthen credibility, and make people pay attention. You know how to help find, nurture, and manage those relationships while keeping advisory agreements, expert content, and ongoing initiatives moving forward.
 You know how to make campaigns measurable. UTMs, GA4, attribution, affiliate links, conversion paths, dashboards—you want the plumbing in place before anyone hits publish. If a campaign launches and nobody can tell where the sales came from, you start developing an eye twitch. You can build clean tracking systems, spot reporting holes, and make sure every partnership has a clear line of sight to performance.
 You know how to manage a budget.  You know when a creator is worth the fee, when the numbers don’t stack up, and when it’s time to negotiate harder, change the deal, or walk away. You pity the fools who throw five figures at an influencer because “their engagement looks really strong.”
 You know how to get campaigns over the finish line. Brief → negotiation → content → compliance → approvals → launch → tracking → reporting → optimization. You’ve managed the whole thing before. You can keep multiple campaigns moving at once, chase down loose ends without becoming everyone’s least favourite Slack notification, and make sure things actually launch on time.
 You keep an eye on the competition. Which creators are competitors using? What offers are they testing? What messages keep showing up? Who seems to be everywhere all of a sudden? You notice the patterns, find the gaps, and turn what you learn into better ideas for us. Not a 53-slide competitor deck that gets presented once and then quietly dies in Google Drive.
 You’re good at getting different people to work together. Creative, paid media, compliance, analytics, external partners—you can keep everyone aligned without turning every decision into a meeting about whether we need another meeting. You communicate clearly, keep momentum high, and generally make complicated things feel less complicated.
 You’ve got the experience to prove you can do all of the above. We’re looking for 3+ years in influencer marketing, affiliate management, partnerships, creator growth, or a similar role. Bonus points if you’ve worked in health, wellness, supplements, D2C, eCommerce, women’s health, or another category where credibility matters just as much as conversion.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you? 
If you’re nodding your head and already thinking about which partners, systems, and campaign levers you’d tackle first, then we can’t wait to meet you.
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble –you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people-smart –in the sense that you’re a great teammate
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal. So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent. So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills and experience, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 Incredible dog-friendly, Yaletown office one block from SkyTrain
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave. Culture is everything to us. Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible. But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant. So, to make sure our future Senior Influencer and Partnerships Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application:
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter. Please read carefully:
 1. Write a cover letter addressing: 
 Why are you the best Senior Influencer and Partnerships Specialist for this role? Give quantifiable examples of related achievements like campaign ROI, ROAS, CAC, incremental sales lift, volume of creators managed, or others that show the impact of your work.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What's the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job: 
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Upload your cover letter and resume 
 Ensure that your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best–and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume.
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read! 
 We are looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly, and you can also expect a prompt response.

Senior Superintendent (Construction) 
 Maple Reinders is currently looking to add a Senior Superintendent to our team based out of Mississauga, Ontario. Projects may be located throughout Ontario across both our Buildings and Civil divisions, including wastewater and water infrastructure, Defence Canada, advanced manufacturing, and food processing facilities.
 As a Senior Superintendent, you will take a lead role in managing multiple field teams, overseeing complex construction projects, and providing senior-level leadership across project sites. Maple Reinders is a growing organization, continually winning new work across diverse sectors, offering new experiences and challenges.
 At Maple Reinders, we look for leaders who can: 
 Direct field operations in the delivery of projects while adhering to schedules, budgets, safety, and risk requirements.

 Develop and execute project work plans aimed at keeping projects on track and on budget.
 Provide senior-level field leadership, manage multiple teams, mentor staff, and support succession planning.
 Lead site operations on complex projects and resolve project challenges proactively.
 We are focused on candidates who currently have: 
 Senior-level Superintendent experience with a General Contractor.
 Experience managing multiple field teams and large construction projects.
 Experience delivering commercial, institutional, industrial, civil, or infrastructure projects.
 Strong leadership, planning, and communication skills.
 Proficiency with MS Office and Windows-based applications.
 Post-secondary construction-related education, CET, or equivalent would be considered an asset.
 About Maple Reinders:

We are a full-service construction provider specializing in  ICI buildings  (industrial, commercial, institutional) and  civil/environmental projects  such as water and wastewater treatment plants, composting facilities, energy-from-waste, and biogas systems.
 With  500+ team members  across six offices nationwide and more than  2,900 projects completed coast-to-coast , we have built a reputation for excellence, adaptability, and integrity.
 We are proud to be:
 A  Platinum Member  of Canada’s Best Managed Companies
 Certified Great Place to Work 
 Recipients of numerous awards for  innovation, sustainability, and design 
 We want an individual who will embody Maple Reinders core values of:
 People  – Supporting employees to thrive.
 Integrity  – Doing the right thing without compromise.
 Relationships  – Building trust with clients & partners.
 Stewardship  – Caring for communities & the environment.
 Ingenuity  – Embracing challenges. Encouraging ideas. Engineering solutions.
 Why you should work here: 
 Competitive Salaries (paid weekly)
 Company branded truck
 Starting at three weeks paid vacation plus additional gifted days off over the Christmas break  
 RRSP with employer matching (up to 5%)
 Discretionary bonuses & profit sharing
 Group Health Insurance Plan (medical, dental, health care spending account)
 Life insurance and disability coverage
 Employee rewards program (Maple Points)
 Discount programs & memberships.
 Employee and Project referral bonuses
 Employee Assistance Program
 Career growth and learning opportunities, including professional certifications.
